title: Fair clustering through fairlets
authors: Flavio Chierichetti, Ravi Kumar, Silvio Lattanzi, Sergei Vassilvitskii
definition: Introduces the *fairlet* decomposition: a clustering is fair if every cluster preserves the population-level ratio of two protected groups (the "balance" notion). Fairness is enforced as a hard constraint on group proportions within each cluster.
contribution: Reduces fair $k$-center and fair $k$-median (with two colors) to first partitioning points into small fair sets (fairlets) and then clustering the fairlet centers, giving the first approximation algorithms for fair clustering with provable guarantees.
open_problems: Extension beyond two protected groups to many colors with tight ratios
Scalability of fairlet decomposition to massive datasets
Fairlets for $k$-means (sum-of-squares) objective

title: Fair algorithms for clustering
authors: Suman Kalyan Bera, Deeparnab Chakrabarty, Nicolas Flores, Maryam Negahbani
definition: Generalizes balance to $(\alpha,\beta)$-proportional fairness: each protected group's representation in every cluster is bounded within $[\beta,\alpha]$ of its overall fraction, supporting multiple, overlapping groups.
contribution: Gives a general framework that converts any vanilla clustering approximation into a fair one with only a small additive violation of the fairness constraints, for $k$-center, $k$-median and $k$-means.
open_problems: Eliminating the additive constraint violation
Lower bounds on the price of fairness for multiple overlapping groups

title: Scalable fair clustering
authors: Arturs Backurs, Piotr Indyk, Krzysztof Onak, Baruch Schieber, Ali Vakilian, Tal Wagner
definition: Adopts the fairlet balance notion of Chierichetti et al. and studies how to compute it at scale.
contribution: Gives a near-linear time algorithm for fairlet decomposition, reducing the cost from quadratic and making balance-based fair clustering practical on large inputs.
open_problems: Near-linear fair clustering for more than two groups
Dynamic / streaming maintenance of fairlets

title: Guarantees for spectral clustering with fairness constraints
authors: Matthäus Kleindessner, Samira Samadi, Pranjal Awasthi, Jamie Morgenstern
definition: Group fairness (balance): every cluster should contain each protected group in roughly its population proportion, here imposed on **spectral** clustering by adding linear group-representation constraints to the eigenvector relaxation.
contribution: First to fold group-fairness constraints into spectral clustering — the fair constraints are absorbed into a constrained eigenproblem, yielding fair spectral embeddings with a theoretical justification and little extra cost.
open_problems: Extending the constrained relaxation cleanly to many (overlapping) protected groups
Individual- rather than group-fairness variants of spectral clustering
Quantifying the fairness–cut-quality trade-off

title: Fair $k$-center clustering for data summarization
authors: Haris Angelidakis, Adam Kurpisz, Leon Sering, Rico Zenklusen
definition: Group fairness as representation constraints for data summarization: when choosing k centers (a summary), each protected group must receive a prescribed number/share of the selected centers.
contribution: Approximation algorithms for $k$-center summarization under per-group representation (cardinality) constraints, balancing summary quality against fair coverage of every group.
open_problems: Handling many simultaneous / overlapping sensitive attributes
Scaling fair summarization to streaming or massive inputs
Tight approximation lower bounds under representation constraints

title: Proportionally fair clustering
authors: Xingyu Chen, Brandon Fain, Liang Lyu, Kamesh Munagala
definition: Proportional fairness (the *core*): any block of at least $n/k$ points that could all move closer to some alternative center has a justified complaint; a clustering is proportionally fair if no such blocking coalition exists.
contribution: Introduces proportional fairness for centroid clustering, proves approximately-proportional (approximate-core) solutions always exist and are computable, and bounds the price of proportional fairness.
open_problems: Whether an exact core solution always exists for $k$-means
Efficient algorithms achieving the best possible proportionality factor
Proportional fairness for non-centroid and correlation clustering

title: Socially fair $k$-means clustering
authors: Mehrdad Ghadiri, Samira Samadi, Santosh S. Vempala
definition: Socially fair (min-max) $k$-means: minimize the maximum average clustering cost over the protected groups, rather than the aggregate cost — protecting the worst-off group.
contribution: Formalizes the socially fair $k$-means objective and gives a practical Lloyd-style algorithm plus approximation analysis, launching the min-max line of work.
open_problems: Tight approximation factor for socially fair $k$-means
Hardness of the min-max objective for many groups

title: Algorithmic fairness datasets: the story so far
authors: Alessandro Fabris, Stefano Messina, Gianmaria Silvello, Gian Antonio Susto
definition: Not a method but a **survey of data**: it catalogs the datasets that algorithmic-fairness research (fair clustering included) is built on, documenting their domains, sensitive attributes and tasks.
contribution: A comprehensive, documented inventory of 200+ fairness datasets — provenance, sensitive attributes, pitfalls and usage — meant to improve data hygiene across the field.
open_problems: Standardised documentation / datasheets for fairness datasets
Clustering-specific benchmark datasets with ground-truth sensitive groups
Assessing representativeness and licensing of widely-reused datasets

title: On the cost of essentially fair clusterings
authors: Ioana Oriana Bercea, Martin Großand Samir Khuller, Aounon Kumar, Clemens Rösner, Daniel R. Schmidt, Melanie Schmidt
definition: “Essentially fair” clustering: each cluster matches the dataset’s group proportions up to a small additive slack — a relaxation of exact balance that admits good approximations.
contribution: A general framework converting standard $k$-center/median/means approximations into fair ones with bounded constraint violation, plus bicriteria guarantees and structural results on the cost of fairness.
open_problems: Removing the additive fairness violation entirely
Tight bounds for many overlapping groups
Lower bounds on the true price of (exact) fairness

title: Coresets for clustering with fairness constraints
authors: Lingxiao Huang, Shaofeng H.-C. Jiang, Nisheeth K. Vishnoi
definition: Group-fair clustering under balance constraints (bounded fraction of each protected color per cluster) for the $k$-means / $k$-median objective.
contribution: The first **coreset** constructions for fair clustering: small weighted summaries that preserve both cost and fairness constraints, making constrained fair clustering scalable.
open_problems: Coreset size lower bounds under fairness constraints
Coresets for many groups without exponential blow-up
Coresets for individually-fair objectives

title: Fair Coresets and Streaming Algorithms for Fair $k$-means
authors: Melanie Schmidt, Chris Schwiegelshohn, Christian Sohler
definition: Fair $k$-means in the fairlet/balance sense: every cluster must preserve the dataset’s group proportions.
contribution: Introduces **fair coresets** — shows any $k$-means coreset can be made fair — and uses them to give the first streaming algorithm for fair $k$-means.
open_problems: Streaming fair clustering with many groups
Fully-dynamic maintenance of fair coresets
Fair coresets for objectives beyond $k$-means

title: Fair clustering via equitable group representations
authors: Mohsen Abbasi, Aditya Bhaskara, Suresh Venkatasubramanian
definition: Equitable group representation: rather than balancing membership, it bounds the **average clustering cost borne by each protected group**, minimizing the worst group’s cost (a min-max / social-fairness notion).
contribution: Formalizes equitable (min-max) group representation for centroid clustering and gives practical algorithms that equalize per-group average cost.
open_problems: Approximation guarantees for the min-max group-cost objective
Behaviour with many or overlapping groups
Reconciling representation-cost fairness with balance fairness

title: An overview of fairness in clustering
authors: Anshuman Chhabra, Karina Masalkovaite, Prasant Mohapatra
definition: A survey: organizes the many fairness notions used in clustering (group/balance, individual, and others) into a common taxonomy.
contribution: A broad overview categorizing fairness definitions, algorithms and evaluation metrics for clustering, mapping how the sub-areas relate.
open_problems: Unifying the proliferating fairness notions
Standard benchmarks and metrics for fair clustering
Bridging theoretical and deep-learning fair clustering

title: Individual fairness for $k$-clustering
authors: Sepideh Mahabadi, Ali Vakilian
definition: Individual fairness for clustering (Jung–Kannan–Lutz style): every point is entitled to a center within its $n/k$ nearest-neighbor radius, so no individual is left far from a center relative to the local density.
contribution: Gives the first approximation algorithms (bicriteria and true) for individually fair $k$-clustering via LP relaxation and rounding.
open_problems: Constant-factor approximation without bicriteria relaxation
Combining individual fairness with group fairness
Scalable individually-fair algorithms

title: Deep fair clustering for visual learning
authors: Peizhao Li, Han Zhao, Hongfu Liu
definition: Group fairness via representation learning: cluster assignments should be statistically independent of the protected attribute, so each cluster stays balanced across groups.
contribution: A deep fair clustering model (DFC) that learns clustering-friendly yet group-invariant representations of images using adversarial / structure-preserving objectives.
open_problems: Theoretical guarantees for deep fair clustering
Handling multiple sensitive attributes jointly
Training stability and reproducibility of the adversarial objective

title: Fair correlation clustering
authors: Sara Ahmadian, Alessandro Epasto, Ravi Kumar, Mohammad Mahdian
definition: Fair correlation clustering: every output cluster must be color-balanced — no protected color exceeds a chosen fraction of any cluster.
contribution: First approximation algorithms for correlation clustering under per-cluster color-balance constraints.
open_problems: Closing the approximation-ratio gap for fair correlation clustering
Many colors with tight ratios
Min-max / social-fairness variants of correlation clustering

title: Fair hierarchical clustering
authors: Sara Ahmadian, Alessandro Epasto, Marina Knittel, Ravi Kumar, Mohammad Mahdian, Benjamin Moseley, Philip Pham, Sergei Vassilvitskii, Yuyan Wang
definition: Fairness for **hierarchical** clustering: every cluster in the tree must be balanced across protected groups, evaluated under Dasgupta’s hierarchical cost.
contribution: Defines fair hierarchical clustering and gives approximation algorithms that build group-balanced dendrograms with bounded Dasgupta cost.
open_problems: Tighter approximations for fair Dasgupta cost
Individual fairness in hierarchies
Scalable fair hierarchical clustering

title: Fair colorful $k$-center clustering
authors: Xinrui Jia, Kshiteej Sheth, Ola Svensson
definition: Fair / colorful $k$-center: points carry colors with per-color coverage requirements; choose centers minimizing the covering radius while meeting every color’s quota (optionally with outliers).
contribution: Improved constant-factor approximations for colorful (fair) $k$-center, including the outlier setting, sharpening earlier pseudo-approximations.
open_problems: Avoiding exponential dependence on the number of colors
Tight approximation factors for fair $k$-center with outliers
Streaming / distributed colorful $k$-center

title: Approximation algorithms for socially fair clustering
authors: Yury Makarychev, Ali Vakilian
definition: Socially fair (min-max) clustering under $\ell_p$ objectives: minimize the largest group-wise cost.
contribution: Provides $O(\log k / \log\log k)$-style approximation guarantees for socially fair $k$-median/$k$-means via LP rounding, and matching hardness, characterizing the price of social fairness.
open_problems: Closing the gap between upper and lower bounds
Polynomial-time constant-factor approximations for fixed number of groups

title: Proportionally fair clustering revisited
authors: Evi Micha, Nisarg Shah
definition: Proportional fairness / the core: any sufficiently large group of points that could collectively reduce their cost by deviating to their own center constitutes a justified complaint; a clustering is proportionally fair (in the core) if no such blocking coalition exists.
contribution: Establishes existence and approximation of proportionally fair (core) solutions for centroid clustering and bounds the price of proportional fairness.
open_problems: Exact core existence for $k$-means
Efficient algorithms achieving the best possible core approximation
Proportional fairness for non-centroid / correlation clustering

title: Fairness in clustering with multiple sensitive attributes
authors: Savitha Sam Abraham, Deepak P, Sowmya S. Sundaram
definition: Group fairness across **multiple** sensitive attributes at once: clusters should be balanced with respect to every protected attribute simultaneously.
contribution: A clustering method (FairKM) that embeds balance across several sensitive attributes into the objective, rather than one attribute at a time.
open_problems: Guarantees when attributes are correlated
Scalability with many attributes
Trade-offs between competing attributes’ fairness

title: Improved approximation algorithms for individually fair clustering
authors: Ali Vakilian, Mustafa Yal\cciner
definition: Individual fairness (each point gets a center within its $n/k$-nearest-neighbor radius) for $k$-median / $k$-means.
contribution: Improved approximation algorithms for individually fair clustering, reducing the cost factor and fairness violation over the original guarantees.
open_problems: Closing the gap to a tight constant factor
Removing bicriteria relaxations
Scalable individually-fair algorithms

title: Better Algorithms for Individually Fair $k$-Clustering
authors: Maryam Negahbani, Deeparnab Chakrabarty
definition: Individual fairness for $k$-clustering: every point deserves a center within the radius of its $n/k$ nearest neighbours.
contribution: Better algorithms for individually fair clustering via LP rounding, improving the approximation ratio for $k$-median / $k$-means with individual-fairness guarantees.
open_problems: Matching approximation lower bounds
Jointly individual- and group-fair clustering
Faster, scalable implementations

title: A center in your neighborhood: Fairness in facility location
authors: Christopher Jung, Sampath Kannan, Neil Lutz
definition: Individual fairness (the neighborhood notion): every point is entitled to a center within the radius that contains its $n/k$ nearest points — no individual may be left disproportionately far from a center.
contribution: Originates individual fairness for clustering / facility location, establishing existence and approximate computation of solutions that honor every point’s fair radius.
open_problems: True constant-factor (non-bicriteria) algorithms
Combining individual with group fairness
Efficient algorithms at scale

title: Hierarchical clustering-based personalized federated learning for robust and fair human activity recognition
authors: Youpeng Li, Xuyu Wang, Lingling An
definition: Fairness across users/clients in federated learning: clustered personalization aims to equalize model quality across heterogeneous users for human-activity recognition.
contribution: A hierarchical-clustering-based personalized federated-learning framework that improves robustness and cross-user fairness in activity recognition.
open_problems: Formal fairness guarantees in clustered federated learning
Scaling to many heterogeneous clients
Privacy–fairness interactions

title: Variational fair clustering
authors: Imtiaz Masud Ziko, Jing Yuan, Eric Granger, Ismail Ben Ayed
definition: Balance fairness expressed as a divergence penalty: each cluster’s group proportions are pushed to match the dataset distribution.
contribution: A general variational framework that adds a fairness (balance) regularizer to existing clustering objectives ($k$-means, spectral, …) and scales to large data.
open_problems: Theoretical balance guarantees for the variational objective
Many groups / continuous sensitive attributes
Tuning the fairness–quality trade-off automatically

title: Probabilistic fair clustering
authors: Seyed A. Esmaeili, Brian Brubach, Leonidas Tsepenekas, John Dickerson
definition: Probabilistic fair clustering: group memberships are known only as probabilities, and balance constraints must hold in expectation / with high probability.
contribution: First algorithms for fair clustering under uncertain (probabilistic) group memberships, with approximation guarantees on cost and expected fairness.
open_problems: Adversarial (worst-case) rather than probabilistic uncertainty
Tight bounds under noisy memberships
Many groups with correlated uncertainty

title: A pairwise fair and community-preserving approach to $k$-center clustering
authors: Brian Brubach, Darshan Chakrabarti, John P. Dickerson, Samir Khuller, Aravind Srinivasan, Leonidas Tsepenekas
definition: Pairwise fairness with community preservation: similar points (same community) should be treated similarly by the clustering, a pairwise/individual-style fairness rather than group balance.
contribution: Introduces a pairwise-fair, community-preserving objective for $k$-center and gives algorithms that respect it.
open_problems: Reconciling pairwise fairness with group balance
Approximation guarantees for the pairwise objective
Scaling community-preserving fair clustering
